# ICP / Persona Draft — ICP-001: The Accountable HQ Publisher

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | ICP-001 |
| Flow Step | 04 — Define ICP / target customer (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | PM-001 |
| Upstream inputs | PS-001 (Problem Statement v3.0), IOH-001 (v1.0), IB-001 (v1.0) |
| Reviewers this run | UXR-001 (independent, post-production); MKT, SALES (supporting) |
| Version | 2.0 (attempt 2 — supersedes v1.0, returned) |
| Status | Draft → for review |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** on the qualification logic and exclusions; **Low** on all counts, prices and weights |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — zero primary interviews, no web/CRM access this run (§9) |
| Gate criteria | **MET** — a narrow, testable segment exists, expressed as a 4-condition screener with hard disqualifiers and pre-registered falsification thresholds (§3, §6, §8) |

---

## 0. What is different in attempt 2

Attempt 1 was returned for low confidence on an evidence-led step. I cannot generate the missing interviews in this run, so asserting the same firmographics more loudly would be dishonest. I have instead changed the *form* of the artifact:

| Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 |
|---|---|
| A described segment ("NGOs and foundations with Bangladesh programmes") — an unverifiable demographic guess | A segment **derived** from four necessity conditions that follow from PS-001's problem structure, so the logic stands or falls on reasoning we can inspect, not on data we don't have |
| Implicitly assumed institutional buyers are the safe segment | Surfaces the **contradiction inside that assumption** (§2) and converts it into the segment's single hard disqualifier (§4) — organizations with a Bangladesh office are *out*, not in |
| No operational test | A **6-question screener with root-cause coding** back to PS-001's P1–P6, plus pre-registered thresholds that will falsify this ICP within 24 interviews (§6, §8) |
| No timing dimension | **Trigger events** — the conditions under which a dormant Bengali mandate becomes a funded project (§7) |

The substantive new contribution is §2. It narrows the segment from "institutions with Bengali audiences" (large, comfortable, wrong) to "institutions with a Bengali *audience* but no Bengali *operational presence*" (small, uncomfortable, defensible).

---

## 1. Necessity conditions (how this ICP was derived)

PS-001 says the blockage is that a Bengali edition is *unverifiable*, *unquantifiable* and *unroutable*, and IOH-001 says our price only survives against buyers not shopping the Dhaka/Kolkata labour market. Four conditions follow. A buyer failing **any one** cannot be an early customer, regardless of how attractive they look.

| ID | Necessity condition | Derived from | If they fail it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N1** | Holds a **hard-currency budget line** for language/publication work **and** a *pre-existing* Bengali audience mandate | IOH R-03/A7 (price anchoring); PS-001 "demand-creation sale" risk | Either they anchor to local rates and we lose on price, or we must create the mandate — a sale we cannot afford at $1,800 ASP |
| **N2** | Has **no in-house or implementing-partner Bengali editorial capacity** | PS-001 §2 counter-evidence (the field-office alternative) | Their true alternative is a ~$400 internal job; we are a rounding error on their org chart, not a vendor |
| **N3** | A **named individual** personally carries reputational exposure if the Bengali reads badly | PS-001 P3 (quality unverifiable) | Nobody will pay a premium for assurance; the deliverable reverts to a commodity file |
| **N4** | Has a **reporting or compliance obligation** that requires evidence of reach | PS-001 P2 + P4 (unquantifiable, unroutable) | The "evidenced" leg of our product is worthless to them and we are competing on price alone |

**INFERENCE — the structural tension that defines the segment:** N1 and N2 are **negatively correlated**. The organizations most likely to have a funded Bengali mandate (large INGOs, multilaterals, big foundations) are precisely those most likely to have a Bangladesh country office or long-standing local implementing partner — i.e. they fail N2. IOH-001's "safest segment" is therefore mostly *disqualified by its own strength*. Our early customers live in the narrow band where **audience is Bengali but operations are not**.

That band is real, and it is where I am pointing discovery.

---

## 2. Primary ICP (ICP-A)

**DECISION D-005 (PM-001, autonomous this run):**

> **ICP-A — the HQ-based publications owner at a mission-driven organization that produces long-form English titles for a Bangladesh, West Bengal or Bengali-diaspora audience it reaches *through third parties*, and that has no Bengali editorial function of its own.**

| Attribute | Value | Claim type |
|---|---|---|
| Organization type | Mission/values-driven publisher, foundation, global-health or literacy body, open-education/OER project, faith or mission agency | INFERENCE from N1–N4 |
| Headcount | **20–500** — large enough for a publications budget, small enough to lack a country editorial office | ESTIMATE (band chosen so N1 and N2 can co-exist) |
| HQ | US, UK, Canada, EU, Nordics, Australia, Gulf | INFERENCE (hard-currency budgeting) |
| Bengali footprint | Audience or partner network only — **no** Bangladesh/India office, no local production staff | INFERENCE (N2) |
| Content shape | Long-form: books, handbooks, curricula, field guides, patient/plain-language guides, training manuals — 20k–100k words, editorially coherent, meant to be *read* | DECISION D-007 (below) |
| Buyer title | Director/Head/Manager of **Publications**, **Communications**, **Programme Learning**, **Knowledge Management**, or **Global Content** | INFERENCE |
| Annual language/translation spend | **$10k–$150k**, grant- or core-funded, USD/GBP/EUR | ESTIMATE — method: a 20–500 person publishing-active org typically carries a translation line of low single-digit % of programme comms budget; entirely unverified |
| Deal shape we expect | 1 pilot title at $1,500–$3,000, then 2–6 titles/yr if the pilot survives internal review | ESTIMATE from IOH-001 §3.1 pricing |

**Two sub-segments to source against, ranked:**

| | Sub-segment | Why ranked here | Hypothesized fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | **Faith / values-based publishers and mission agencies** (US/UK/CA HQ, distributing through local partners) | Buy reach as *mission*, so PS-001's P2 (unquantifiable ROI) barely binds — they do not need an ROI case. Long history of commissioning language editions. Named accountable publisher exists (N3). Rarely have local editorial staff (N2). | **Highest** |
| **A2** | **Global-health, literacy and OER content owners** (guideline bodies, disease/patient foundations, textbook and open-curriculum projects) | Strongest N4 — grant and evaluation reporting *demands* evidence of localized reach, which is the leg competitors don't sell. Plain-language and accuracy obligations make P3 (verification) acute and expensive to get wrong. | High |

**DECISION D-007 (scope, autonomous):** for ICP purposes, "book" means **any long-form English title of 20k–100k words intended to be read end to end**, including institutional handbooks and curricula. Rationale: the production line in IOH-001 D-002 is identical, and this materially widens a segment that would otherwise be too thin to test in six weeks. This is a **deliberate widening of the wedge, not of the product**; the deliverable spec is unchanged (translated + edited + typeset + EPUB/print + metadata + channel). Flagged for CPO-001/CEO-001 dissent because it edges toward IOH's H3.

---

## 3. Parallel probe (ICP-B) — one probe only

> **ICP-B — the owner of institutional learning content with a *signed or short-pipeline* Bangladesh/West Bengal deployment**: courseware, EdTech, corporate L&D, professional-certification body.

Kept as a probe (≈20% of interview slots) because it shares the pipeline, tests IOH's H3 wallet, and its N4 is contractual rather than aspirational. **Not primary**, because procurement cycles will outrun our six-week discovery window and would starve us of evidence at exactly the wrong moment.

---

## 4. Exclusions — who is explicitly NOT the ICP

Each exclusion names the failed necessity condition. These are hard filters for Step 05 sourcing, not preferences.

| Excluded | Fails | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Large INGOs / UN agencies / multilaterals with Bangladesh country offices or standing local partners** | **N2** | Their alternative is an internal field-office job at local cost. This is the single most important exclusion in this artifact and it deliberately overrides IB-001's "Segment A = P0". Country-office orgs are a **later channel partner**, not an early payer. |
| **Bangladeshi and Indian publishers** (Dhaka / Kolkata trade houses) | N1 | Priced to local labour. Confirms IB-001's P2 ranking. Channel, not customer. |
| **International self-published & mid-list authors** (IB-001 Segment B) | **N3, N4** | No reputational structure that makes assurance purchasable, no reporting obligation that makes evidence purchasable, and a rational ROI test on Bengali retail revenue probably fails at *any* price. Testing them first would falsify our price thesis while teaching us nothing about PS-001's real blockers. **DECISION D-006: excluded from initial outbound; revisit only if ICP-A fails.** |
| **Trade publishers holding third-party translation rights** | N1 + P6 | Rights-committee friction dominates; sales cycle measured in quarters. |
| **Academic authors / individual researchers** | N1 | No budget line, no signature authority. |
| **Organizations wanting Bengali *interpretation*, subtitling, app-string or short-form marketing localization** | Product fit | Different production line, different competitors (Smartling-class). Out of scope. |
| **Any buyer who cannot warrant they hold translation rights** | Legal | Per IOH A3 / GC-001: rights warranty is a precondition
